title: PPipe: Efficient Video Analytics Serving on Heterogeneous GPU Clusters via Pool-Based Pipeline Parallelism
problem: Efficient serving of latency-bound model inference on heterogeneous GPU clusters where GPUs have vastly different computational capabilities. Current systems underutilize lower-tier GPUs despite many CNN layers executing with comparable latency across different GPU classes.
motivation: Heterogeneous GPU clusters are increasingly commonplace in public clouds and data centers, but existing serving systems fail to exploit the synergy between model layer diversity and GPU hardware diversity.
method: PPipe uses pool-based pipeline parallelism to assign model layers to GPU classes based on per-layer latency profiles. An MILP-based control plane optimizes task assignments while the data plane implements resource reservation-based adaptive batching to maintain pipeline throughput and latency bounds.
key_novelty: Applying pipeline parallelism (traditionally for training throughput) to latency-bound inference serving by exploiting comparable per-layer execution times across heterogeneous GPU classes.
contributions: Demonstrates pipeline parallelism enables effective serving on heterogeneous GPU clusters through layer-to-GPU assignment
Proposes PPipe with MILP-based control plane and pool-based pipeline scheduling mechanism
Introduces resource reservation-based adaptive batching for maintaining pipeline throughput
Achieves 32.2%-75.1% higher serving throughput with 41.1%-65.5% better low-class GPU utilization on 18 CNN models
primary_theme: efficient serving on heterogeneous gpu clusters
